summary: Intermittent 403 on presigned artifact range downloads caused by egress appliance header rewrite + source-NAT pool
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports intermittent 403 errors when Redwood-serving nodes attempt to fetch model artifact range downloads (HTTP 206 range requests) using presigned S3 URLs. Errors started after a network change on BrightCart side (new egress inspection appliance rollout). Impact: model pulls fail ~2-8% of range requests, causing streaming stalls and increased retries; customer sees elevated tail latency and occasional model load failures. Hypothesis: egress appliance is performing a combination of source-NAT to a limited EIP pool and HTTP header/SNI rewrite for caching/inspection; this is altering the request seen by S3 (Host/SNI/ALPN or range semantics), causing SigV4 / signature validation or range handling to fail intermittently.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private Redwood deployment in BrightCart VPC (prod-us-east).
2) Trigger a large model artifact fetch that results in ranged GETs (>20MB) from serving node behind corporate egress appliance.
3) Observe intermittent 403 responses on range requests from the artifact URL while full GETs sometimes succeed.
4) Repeat under controlled lab with appliance in-passive/active mode to correlate failure rate.
logs: [2026-03-09T15:12:07Z] http-outbound: Host header changed from 'redwood-artifacts-us-east.s3.amazonaws.com' to 'corp-cache.local' (observed in tcpdump on node)
[2026-03-09T15:12:07Z] aws-sigv4: string-to-sign verification failed for chunked/ranged GET (client-ip: 198.51.100.45 -> seen-by-s3: 203.0.113.12)
VPC Flow Log sample (node egress): version=2 srcaddr=10.10.3.12 dstaddr=52.216.0.1 srcport=45910 dstport=443 protocol=6 packets=12 bytes=16384 action=ACCEPT log-status=OK
Egress appliance NAT log: original-src=10.10.3.12 translated-src=198.51.100.45 pool-id=egress-pool-7 cache-hit=true host-rewrite=true
investigation_notes: Mar 10 09:10 - Triage call with BrightCart (#support-brightcart). Customer confirmed new egress appliance (vendor: NetGuardEdge v4.2) rolled out on 2026-03-08 across prod subnets.

Mar 10 10:05 - Captured tcpdump on serving node during reproducer: observed TLS ClientHello SNI 'redwood-artifacts-us-east.s3.amazonaws.com' in some flows, but in failing flows the SNI was rewritten to 'corp-cache.local' and Host header inside decrypted HTTP/2 stream (post-mitm) was 'corp-cache.local'.

Mar 10 11:20 - Correlated failure windows with egress NAT pool exhaustion: NAT pool rotates translated-src among ~8 EIPs; S3 observed requests from multiple EIPs but some EIPs were also used by corporate cache, causing cached 403 responses to be returned upstream for ranged GETs.

Mar 10 12:45 - Reproduced in lab by enabling 'http host-rewrite for cache' in appliance – observed same 403s on ranged requests; full-file downloads succeeded more often because cache returned 200 for full object but range requests relied on correct SigV4/headers and were rejected.

Mar 10 14:00 - SRE ran 'curl -I --range 0-1023 <presigned-url>' from node with and without HTTP/CONNECT tunneling: when CONNECT bypassed inspection, 206 returned consistently; when proxied and host-rewrite enabled, 403 returned rapidly with x-amz-error-code=SignatureDoesNotMatch.

Mar 11 08:30 - Opened ticket with appliance vendor (TICKET-NGE-1129) and AWS Support (SR-987654321) to validate whether host/SNI rewrite + client IP translation could cause signature verification failures for ranged GETs.

Mar 11 13:15 - AWS confirmed that altering Host header/SNI for signed URL requests will invalidate SigV4 verification; caching appliances that rewrite Host for internal cache keys can therefore return stale/incorrect responses for presigned URLs.
comments: Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-10: Received initial report from BrightCart: intermittent model load timeouts. Created ticket and scheduled triage.
BrightCart-ops (customer) 2026-03-10: We deployed NetGuardEdge across all egress subnets on 2026-03-08. Rolling back is expensive; looking for mitigations.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10: Captured tcpdump and vpc flow logs; see investigation_notes. Suspect host-rewrite + NAT translation interplay. Requesting customer's firewall team to disable Host header rewrite for s3.amazonaws.com domains as a temporary mitigation.
NetGuardEdge support 2026-03-11: Confirmed appliance has 'cache key normalization' feature that rewrites Host; provided config flags to disable host rewrite for a domain whitelist.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-11: Pushed config change on customer's test subnet to whitelist *.s3.amazonaws.com -> host-rewrite disabled. Observed 0% 403 on range requests for 4-hour window. Customer to schedule prod rollout.

Engineering (Artifact Service) 2026-03-12: Raised GH PR to add resilient retry for transient 403 on ranged artifact downloads with stricter validation for 206 vs 403 (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8291).
resolution: Workaround applied: BrightCart disabled Host header rewrite/caching for *.s3.amazonaws.com on NetGuardEdge and expanded NAT pool allocation to avoid pool exhaustion. After change, ranged artifact failures dropped to <0.1%. Permanent fix: customer to deploy appliance whitelist for Redwood artifact domains and enable pass-through (no host/SNI rewrite) for signed URLs. Engineering added a conservative retry on 403 for range downloads (PR 8291) while we recommend customer changes. Close plan: monitor for 72 hours then move to 'Resolved' if stable.
